incidents.SUMMARY: The governed pre-migration verified backup (backup 2026-10-02_183040-c54f8cb8) completed its 2h07m dump, then failed before any database mutation at the first digest query with: snapshot does not exist (CRITICAL_DIGEST_QUERY_FAILED:trade.decision). Production stayed at schema 067.
incidents.ROOT_CAUSE: The exported snapshot is held by one idle psql session in an open transaction for the whole dump. That session disappeared between 20:37:50Z (dump complete) and 20:42:00Z (failure). Two candidate causes, not distinguishable from the persisted evidence: (1) a long-idle connection reaped on the network path; (2) a transient server-side connectivity event: ops.runtime_worker_cycle recorded a POSTGRES_57P03 (cannot_connect_now) failure at 20:41:47Z, 13 s before the backup failed. The server idle_in_transaction_session_timeout is 1 day and pg_postmaster_start_time is unchanged (2026-09-22), so an idle-transaction timeout and a full restart are ruled out.
incidents.FIX_LIMITS: The heartbeat addresses cause (1) only. It cannot keep a snapshot alive across a server-side connection loss (cause 2). A keeper that dies during a multi-hour dump still forces a rerun; the new assertion makes that failure immediate and explicit. Possible further hardening (not yet implemented): run the digest queries and the schema dump before the long custom dump so the snapshot only needs to survive minutes.
incidents.CURRENT_STATUS: MITIGATED_AND_CONFIRMED_ON_THE_HAPPY_PATH: with the heartbeat and early detection, two governed backups (2026-10-02_205959 and 2026-10-03_023612) completed their dumps and digests; a server-side connection loss during a dump would still force a rerun, now detected immediately with an explicit cause.
incidents.FIX_NOTE: 3158c61: heartbeat keeps the keeper active and records its death; a later commit adds Assert-ThetaSnapshotKeeperAlive, which fails the backup immediately after the dump with the real cause

incidents.SUMMARY: After one transient POSTGRES_57P03 (database cannot accept connections) at 20:41:47Z the Windows worker entered database recovery mode and never left it: no worker cycle ran from 20:41Z until a supervisor restart at about 00:00Z next day. Every recovery probe returned HTTP 503 POSTGRES_CHECKED_OUT_CLIENT_LOST while the database itself was healthy.
incidents.ROOT_CAUSE: withRuntimePostgresClient passed operations a discard() callback that set the same flag used to detect a lost connection, so discard() after a SUCCESSFUL SELECT 1 made the function throw POSTGRES_CHECKED_OUT_CLIENT_LOST. The runtime-db-probe handler calls discard() on purpose (each recovery proof must use a brand-new connection), so the probe could never succeed, the four-success recovery requirement could never be met, and the circuit stayed open. The path had never been exercised against a real outage.
incidents.CURRENT_STATUS: FIXED_AND_RELEASED: shipped in 5006cda; recovery has not yet been exercised by a real outage after the fix. Until then the only proof of the fix is the unit/regression test and the earlier supervisor restart that restored cycles.
incidents.PRODUCTION_MUTATION: NONE (supervisor stop/start only; execution gate LOCKED throughout, zero broker mutations)

incidents.SUMMARY: The post-migration verified backup (2026-10-02_234643-15402cd3) completed its dump and digests, and its real restore matched on structure fingerprint (156 tables, 407 indexes, 116 triggers) and on every table row count and critical-data digest, but the restore test reported dataRowcountParity FAIL, so the governed checkpoint recorded MIGRATION_CHECKPOINT_FAILED. Migration 068 itself was already applied and verified; the pre-migration verified backup is preserved as the known-good restore point.
incidents.ROOT_CAUSE: Restore-Theta.ps1 required the sequence state captured after the dump to equal the restored sequence state exactly. Sequences are not transactional and not part of the exported snapshot, so a live system advances them while a two-hour dump runs (ops.runtime_worker_event_worker_event_id_seq, market.option_quote_snapshot_snapshot_id_seq and others, written by the running worker). The first governed backup passed only because the worker was wedged during it (see INC-20261003-DB-RECOVERY-PROBE). Any backup taken while the worker runs would fail the same way.
incidents.FIX_LIMITS: none known; the check is monotonic (restored sequence values must not exceed the later-captured source values).
incidents.CURRENT_STATUS: FIXED_RELEASED_AND_CONFIRMED: shipped in 35654f2; the governed verified backup 2026-10-03_023612-c03d5f99 ran with the worker active and passed real-restore verification (structure, data row counts, sequences and critical digests); it is the latest verified backup and carries schema head 068_action_plan_integrity.
incidents.PRODUCTION_MUTATION: NONE (read-only dump and an isolated local restore)
